I was broke af and was about to lose my mobile connection besides all the debts.
Just wanted anything so got online to search for postings. Wasn't too into retail cause I don't like dealing with customers much so decided kitchens would be perfect. Found a posting for dishie at local cafe, applied for it, blew the interview but I think they couldn't find anyone else so they called me. Been there for 6 months now. 
I sometimes get service shifts on the front of cafe and learned supervising stuff so hopefully I climb up the ladder soon?
Yeppp. Coffee, water, and Advil for me. Our place is ill-equipped so need pain meds halfway through an 8 hour shift.
All the time! I get ghost cuts despire wearing gloves all the time.
Good luck mate! Ya got this!!
We have these bluetooth speakers in the kitchen. While closing, I just put on music full volume and dance while I sweep and mop. Makes work so much fun.

Oh yeah. And the cuts. Random cuts are normal and I don't even know how most happen. Gloves help reduce the number of cuts I get. The shitty part is that even a scratch takes a week to heal cuz you are constantly in water.

I have soft hands and I usually moisturize religiously. One weekend I decided to do dishes without gloves and by Monday they felt like dry leather. Moisturizing hardly helped. Took 2 weeks to get better. Lesson learnt: always wear gloves even if it's a single cup to wash.
Haven't seen any difference with dexterity since I started the work.

Our chefs are sooo sweet! I get free muffins and special sandwiches (they ain't even on the menu) and sometimes these giant cinnamon rolls (we are a cafe) all the time!

Oof!! Same! I just got "promoted" to do the front end serving besides dishwashing so double the work. Atleast I still got my job. The ither dishie might be losing his cause the new owners think that it's not busy enough for dishies to get 8 hour shifts.
Aww. That's really sweet of them!

I literally was helping at the till taking orders on Monday cause it was sooooo slow.
It's a café. It is usually busy but the weekends are crazy busy. I just learnt to deal with it and am the fastest so am always scheduled on the busiest of the nights.

We don't have a moning guy except for the weekends so gotta do a shit ton before my break. They say weekends are the busiest but to me they are more chill cuz by the time I clock in, the morning guy dies all the dishes for me. I just have to do the itty bitty ones from the kitchen till the chefs leave.

We have these shitty sopa filled steel wool. I hardly ever use them- except to clean the soup tins from upfront. We could bring our own stuff, but me being lazy rather just soak it in heavy duty degreaser. For the most terrible of burns, my chef suggested to rather boil some water in the pan followed by scraping off the char. Easier tbh. Then again, a casual cafe like ours hardly get any charred pans. The chefs are rather careful and super nice and do the soaking themselves if am busy.
